title: Seattle Mariners to Promote Top 100 Prospect to Major Leagues
description: Lazaro Montes, the Mariners power-hitting outfield prospect, will be getting his big league break.
fullText:
The Seattle Mariners are coming off a disappointing sweep at the hands of the Toronto Blue Jays this weekend at the Rogers Centre in Toronto.

The series sweep was accentuated with a 7-0, shutout loss against the Blue Jays on Sunday, which capped off the first leg of a six-game road trip for the Mariners.

The next leg of Seattle's road trip will be against the Boston Red Sox, with game one set to begin at 3:45 p.m. PT on Monday at Fenway Park in Boston.

During the series, the Mariners will be joined by one of the potent power hitters in the minor leagues.

According to a report on "X" from baseball reporter Francys Romero, which was later corroborated by Seattle Times reporter Ryan Divish, Seattle will be calling up top 100 prospect/outfielder Lazaro Montes when active major league rosters expand from 26 to 28 players Sept. 1.

Montes is ranked as the 56th prospect in baseball per MLB Pipeline and has developed a reputation as one of, if not the best home run hitter, in the minor leagues.

Montes began the season with the Double-A Arkansas Travelers before he was promoted to the Triple-A Tacoma Rainiers on July 7.

Since being promoted to Triple-A, Montes has slashed .274/.369/.571 with a .940 OPS in 44 games and has hit 13 doubles and 13 home runs with 30 RBIs.

Across the entire season, the 6-foot-5, 250-pound outfielder .249/.369/.558 with a .927 OPS in 123 games and has hit 24 doubles, a triple and 38 homers and 96 RBIs.

Lazaro Montes with his 24th double. pic.twitter.com/YjEYh5w64p

Montes first joined the Mariners organization as an international free agent out of Cuba on Jan. 15, 2022. He was a part of a stacked international recruiting class that also included fellow top 100 prospect, infielder/outfielder Michael Arroyo.

The 21-year-old mainly plays right field, and hits left-handed, both roles currently handled by on-and-off designated hitters Dominic Canzone and Taylor Ward.

Ward, who's provided some right-handed hitting coverage on the team's roster, has struggled since the team acquired him in a trade with the Baltimore Orioles on Aug. 3.

Canzone has received more regular at-bats against left-handed pitchers. According to an article from Seattle Times reporter Adam Jude, Montes is expected to receive regular at-bats with Seattle, which will likely lead to lineups with both Canzone and Montes in them.

Following their loss against Toronto, the Mariners are five games out of first place in the American League West and five games out of the final wild card spot in the American League.

title: Titans release $3M dual-threat quarterback in a surprising move after cutting Will Levis
description: The Tennessee Titans made some surprising decisions with their QB room on Sunday. After cutting Will Levis it seemed like the QB room was set, but that was not the case.
fullText:
Titans release $3M dual-threat quarterback in a surprising move after cutting Will Levis originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Tennessee Titans are looking to take somewhat of a step forward under Robert Saleh in his first year as head coach. However, it will not be easy, as they still have a young roster that they hope will mature as the season progresses.

On Sunday, Tennessee had to make several decisions, just like the rest of the league. The Titans finally cut ties with Will Levis in a move that felt overdue.

"Will Levis was at one time the hopeful future of the Tennessee Titans at quarterback, but that time has passed and he's leaving Nashville. The No. 33 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Levis is being waived by Tennessee, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Sunday. The team later announced the news," NFL.com's Grant Gordon wrote.

The move to release Levis seemed to open the door for former Tennessee Volunteer Hendon Hooker.

"Tennessee Football legend Hendon Hooker looked to have made the Tennessee Titans' 53-man roster, but that wouldn't be the case. The former Volunteer quarterback was going to survive a crowded quarterback room to earn his spot on the roster after it seemed he notably beat out former Kentucky Wildcat and 2nd-round pick Will Levis to make the roster," SI's Major Passons wrote.

However, that was far from the reality. Tennessee also decided to move on from Hooker, releasing two quarterbacks on the same day. It was a surprising move, and one that SI's Caleb Sisk called a joke.

"The Titans ended up cutting Hendon Hooker anyways… what a joke," Sisk posted.

The Titans will likely try to sign Hooker to the practice squad if he clears waivers, but it is risky to have only one backup quarterback on the roster. Tennessee is in an interesting position heading into the regular season.

Hooker has made $3 million in his career so far. He also had a solid preseason, which is another factor in why this decision was perceived as shocking. Despite his performance, the Titans ultimately decided to move in a different direction at quarterback.

title: Steelers Make Decision on QB Room for 2026 Season
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a decision on who to keep at quarterback ahead of the 2026 season.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have decided to carry all four quarterbacks heading into the 2026 season: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar, and Will Howard.

Rodgers will be the starter as he enters his final season in the league. The 42-year-old completed 65.7 percent of his passes for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in the 2025 season for the Steelers.

The four-time MVP is no longer in his prime, but he is still an accurate passer and led Pittsburgh to an AFC North title and a playoff appearance last season.

Behind Rodgers, the Steelers have veteran Mason Rudolph as the backup. Rudolph has completed 64.4 percent of his passes for 4,925 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions in his six years in the league. He should be a stable backup behind Rodgers.

Pittsburgh's future quarterback could be either Will Howard or Drew Allar. Howard is entering his second year in the league and had a prolific 2024 season at Ohio State. In that campaign, he completed 73 percent of his passes for 4,010 yards, 35 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions while rushing for 226 yards and seven touchdowns.

In the preseason, Howard completed 26 of 40 passes for 229 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions.

Allar had a solid collegiate career at Penn State as a three-year starter, completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 7,402 yards, 61 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions while adding 732 yards and 12 touchdowns on the ground.

Allar was solid in the preseason, completing 30 of 54 passes for 351 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.

Howard and Allar both showed flashes in the preseason, and one of them could develop into the future starter for the Steelers.

Pittsburgh has a talented roster heading into the 2026 season as they look to win a second-straight division title and make it back to the playoffs. However, they have a new head coach, with Mike McCarthy taking over for Mike Tomlin.

With Rodgers' familiarity with McCarthy, the Steelers should be competitive despite the talent of other AFC North teams, including the Baltimore Ravens and Cincinnati Bengals.

title: Bills Release 9-Year Veteran WR as 53-Man Roster Set
description: The Buffalo Bills have named their 53-man roster and the team released a veteran wide receiver who had a good camp. The post Bills Release 9-Year Veteran WR as 53-Man Roster Set appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills have named their 53-man roster.

Buffalo announced their roster cuts on Sunday evening, and one of the notable cuts was veteran wide receiver Trent Sherfield. The Bills brought back Sherfield on a one-year deal, and he was competing for a roster spot, but obviously didn't do enough.

Bills insider Alex Brasky of SI revealed that Sherfield is a practice squad candidate for Buffalo to add more depth at receiver.

"Also interesting that Trent Sherfield has been cut. Might be an option for the practice squad," Brasky wrote on X.

Sherfield played for the Bills in 2023. In his lone year with Buffalo, Sherfield recorded 11 receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown. He's entering his ninth NFL season and spent last season between the Denver Broncos and Arizona Cardinals, and also ended the year on the New England Patriots' practice squad during the playoffs.

In his NFL career, Sherfield has appeared in 124 games, recording 89 receptions for 1,034 yards and 6 touchdowns.

After Sherfield bounced around three different teams last year, he knew he needed to find stability.

He ended up signing a one-year deal with the Bills, which he was excited about as he called it a full-circle moment.

"It's been tough, not going to lie," Sherfield told GNN Sports after practice Monday. "Last year was really tough. First time being cut in eight years. … It was a lot of moving around. It was really tough on me mentally, obviously tough on my family too. But I think it's a full-circle moment coming back here."

Sherfield, meanwhile, said after getting cut by the Broncos, his perspective on his future changed.

"A lot of people get cut. Top guys get released all the time and I think it's just a perspective change," Sherfield said. "… My perspective has changed a lot. … I just told myself that I wasn't going to allow my career to end like that. I've always told myself that I want to go out on my own terms and that the league would never push me out."

Sherfield signed as an undrafted free agent in 2018 with the Cardinals.

title: Sean McVay on Aaron Donald: We'll see if we think it’s best to play him in Australia
description: Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play?
fullText:
Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play?

Head coach Sean McVay didn't rule out Donald potentially playing in Australia when the Rams open the season against the 49ers. But he also didn't want to put a timetable on anything for the three-time AP defensive player of the year.

"I'm not going to talk about any sort of plans, it's going to be a day at a time for us," McVay said in his Sunday press conference. "What does that mean for Australia? The first step was, alright, if you're coming back, let's do that, let's get you back on the practice field, let's get you acclimated to your teammates, to your coaches. And then we'll see what that ramp-up period looks like, whether or not he's available or whether or not we think it's best to play him in Australia. I think the best way to do it is take it one day at a time.

"But, we're obviously excited to be able to have him back."

As he has throughout the summer, McVay noted how much Donald means to him personally when discussing his enthusiasm for the defensive tackle's return.

"It's way bigger than football," McVay said. "There's a lot of history. There's a lot of experiences that we've shared. A lot of love for each other's families. So, I know for him to want to be able to explore this and come back into the mix is a real credit to the special people that he's got a chance to be around, and that's his teammates, and that's obviously his coaches. And excited to start this journey.

So how did it get to this point?

"I think he wanted to get to a point where he knows just from his previous experiences, alright, I want to be able to be there, be a part of the football team, and I think there were some things that he wanted to be able to work through — just in terms of his workouts and where he felt his body was before he could comfortably get to this spot," McVay said. "And so, that was really what went into it.

"He and I both kind of had an unspoken understanding like, once we get the roster down, where are you at with it? You don't owe us anything. And no matter what, there's a lot of love. We wanted to make sure that he felt good about doing that. He obviously is incredibly — his priority is with his family. And so when he does something, he does it all in. That's what led to being able to get it done today."

title: Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster
description: A Seahawks Hard Knocks favorite reportedly survived final cuts after going from substitute teaching and real estate back to an NFL roster. The post Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks are officially keeping one of the breakout personalities from their season of HBO's Hard Knocks.

Wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. has made Seattle's initial 53-man roster,the team announced on Sunday, August 30, as the team worked through its final cuts.

For Foster, making the team would complete one of the more unlikely journeys on Seattle's roster. He went from an undrafted rookie whose first NFL opportunity ended because of injury, to substitute teaching and selling real estate, to becoming one of the players viewers have gotten to know during Hard Knocks.

And unlike many feel-good training camp stories, this one appears to have ended with a roster spot.

Foster's path back to Seattle became a featured storyline during Episode 3 of Hard Knocks.

The Seahawks' official recap noted that Foster spent time with Seattle as an undrafted free agent in 2025 before an injury derailed his first opportunity. After leaving the team, Foster returned home, worked as a substitute teacher and earned his real estate license before eventually getting another opportunity with the Seahawks.

That story continued to get television time as Foster fought for a roster spot.

Gregg Bell of The News Tribune reported that Foster had even substituted at his former high school, St. Edward in Ohio, including an assignment covering a Latin class despite acknowledging he did not know Latin.

His NFL comeback was about more than a television storyline, however.

Foster caught five passes for 36 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's first preseason game, then added receptions of 24 and 13 yards over the Seahawks' final two exhibitions. He finished the preseason with seven catches for 73 yards and a touchdown.

That production gave the Seahawks a football reason to keep him after Hard Knocks gave fans a reason to root for him.

title: Packers Place Former 3rd-Round Pick on Injured Reserve
description: One of the big questions facing the Green Bay Packers was who and how many wide receivers would make the roster. As it turns out, the team will place a second-year wide receiver on the Injured Reserve with a designation to return. This will free up a roster spot for the team, allowing them to […] The post Packers Place Former 3rd-Round Pick on Injured Reserve appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
One of the big questions facing the Green Bay Packers was who and how many wide receivers would make the roster. As it turns out, the team will place a second-year wide receiver on the Injured Reserve with a designation to return. This will free up a roster spot for the team, allowing them to keep an extra wide receiver.

Savion Williams suffered an ankle injury in the Packers' second preseason game against the Denver Broncos. He will now miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season, as the team will ease him back in.

The Packers' wide receiver room was deep. They had their three starters set. Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, and Christian Watson were going to start for the team. Then, they had Williams, Skyy Moore, Bo Melton, J.Michael Sturdivant, Isaiah Neyor, and Will Sheppard.

Green Bay wound up releasing Neyor and Sheppard. They placed Williams on the IR, allowing them to keep Moore, Melton, and Sturdivant as the last three receivers on the depth chart.

All three provide special teams value. Moore is going to be their return option. Melton is the team's top special teams gunner, and Sturdivant made the team with a strong ability to make plays on special teams.

Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst discussed the possibility of keeping seven receivers on the roster. He noted that the team had done it before, but it is an uncommon strategy. Williams not being healthy enough put him in a position where the team did not need to make that decision.

For Williams, it puts the brakes on what was expected to be a year where we learn what he really can bring to the table. He was a third-round pick, but fell to 87th overall because of questions about his usage and role. His first year did not quite ease concerns.

The versatile playmaker had just 11 rushes for 37 yards and 10 targets for 78 yards. His average target depth was 1.7 yards down the field, so he was not bringing much to the passing game. Green Bay was expected to put more on his plate in year two.

With the top three receivers defined in their roles, the team was expected to use Williams as the ultimate gadget weapon. Now, the gadget player missed the last week of the preseason and is going to miss the next four weeks. It will be even harder to integrate him into the offense when he gets back, given his specific role on the offense.

It is not going to completely derail the second-year of Williams, but it is going to put things on pause for what felt like a make-or-break season.

title: Undrafted Patriots Rookie Earns Roster Spot With Unusual Position Switch
description: Undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin learned a second position during the preseason, and that unusual move helped him claim a spot on the Patriots’ initial roster.
fullText:
Undrafted Patriots Rookie Earns Roster Spot With Unusual Position Switch originally appeared on NESN. 

Tanner Arkin found a creative path onto the New England Patriots' initial 53-man roster.

The undrafted rookie arrived as a tight end, impressed as an in-line blocker and then expanded his responsibilities by taking preseason snaps at fullback. That versatility helped Arkin survive Sunday's roster deadline.

The Patriots kept Arkin alongside Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon and fullback Reggie Gilliam, according to the team's position-by-position roster breakdown. New England released tight ends C.J. Dippre and Jack Westover.

Arkin began generating attention early in training camp because of his blocking. He eventually received first-team opportunities in early-down and short-yardage packages, an encouraging sign for any undrafted rookie trying to make an NFL roster.

The Patriots then gave him work at fullback during the preseason.

His performance there was not flawless, but it revealed how New England could use him. Arkin can provide depth behind Gilliam, contribute on field goals and kickoff returns and potentially enter the game in run-heavy packages near the goal line or in short-yardage situations. He also gives offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels another option for preserving two-back formations if Gilliam is unavailable.

Arkin is unlikely to become a major receiving option with Henry and Raridon ahead of him at tight end. His route to playing time will depend on blocking, special teams and his ability to line up in multiple spots. That may sound like a limited role, but it can be extremely valuable for a team trying to maximize every game-day roster position.

Keeping a fourth conventional tight end would have been difficult to justify. Keeping a player who can function as a tight end, emergency fullback and special teams blocker is a different proposition.

Arkin's roster spot also offers another clue about how the Patriots could structure their offense. New England has invested in its running game with Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and newly acquired Corey Kiner, while the offensive line enters the season with far more stability than it has had in recent years.

Having Gilliam and Arkin available gives McDaniels the personnel to use heavier formations and force defenses to account for multiple rushing possibilities.

Undrafted players rarely make a roster by remaining one-dimensional. Arkin recognized his opportunity, embraced an unfamiliar assignment and turned it into a job.

Now the Patriots have an intriguing hybrid player whose value may extend well beyond the traditional tight end depth chart.

title: J.J. McCarthy Issued Compelling Dolphins Trade Idea Amid Vikings’ Decision
description: On Aug. 30, the Minnesota Vikings announced their 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. Moreover, the team’s intriguing decision was to go with four QBs, including J.J. McCarthy.
fullText:
On Aug. 30, the Minnesota Vikings announced their 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. Moreover, the team's intriguing decision was to go with four QBs, including J.J. McCarthy.McCarthy looks to be QB3 behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. With Murray and Wentz having an injury history, McCarthy might be an insurance policy in case injuries hit both. However, the Vikings might know that the former first-round pick has some trade value.Any team needing QB help during the season leading up to the trade deadline might call the Vikings over McCarthy. For Mark Powell of FanSided, the Miami Dolphins make sense for the Vikings QB.In an Aug. 30 article, Powell proposed a trade that would see the Dolphins acquire McCarthy in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick. Miami already landed quarterback Kyle McCord in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick. As a result, Miami probably didn't want to spend much on a backup QB, but if they run into any issues under center, perhaps McCarthy might be an option. "Dumping a former first-round pick is never easy," Powell wrote. "Still, the Dolphins fourth rounder is essentially a late Day 2 pick (since it could very well be the first pick in that round). "The Vikings are a quarterback away from making the postseason, which is why their decision to draft McCarthy, and punt on Kirk Cousins and eventually Sam Darnold, all the more confusing. That is neither here nor there."

As for the Dolphins, they appear content with their two-QB setup for now and will address any issues midseason. Still, Powell argues that someone like McCarthy would be a more reliable option than McCord, who lacks experience in regular-season games. McCord signed with the Packers in January after spending the 2025 season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad after they selected him in the sixth round of last year's draft."Willis is a dual-threat quarterback, which is exciting but also makes him prone to hard contact," Powell added in his article. "I might recommend a veteran backup — which McCarthy is not — but I also wouldn't be tanking as heavily as Jon-Eric Sullivan."

For now, it appears the Dolphins are going with two QBs, but that doesn't mean another team can't call Minnesota for McCarthy. For now, he'll just have to work behind the scenes until an opportunity comes, whether it's in Minnesota or elsewhere.The former Michigan Wolverines product didn't play the preseason finale due to injury, and former NFL player Chad Johnson believes that being injury-prone could be what dooms McCarthy. "I don't know how serious his ankle injury was, but one of the issues that he does have is that he's been injured most of the time since he's been there," Johnson said on the Aug. 28 edition of "Nightcap." "Here we go, we're in the preseason, and you're injured again. "Maybe he thinks his spot is safe. He's one of the few who needs to come in and be playing in a game like this to show that he still has it, because he might be auditioning as well for another team."

fullText:
The Green Bay Packers had a plan for running back throughout the course of the 2026 NFL offseason. Unfortunately, Josh Jacobs getting arrested in May on five charges, including a felony. Obviously, this threw a possible wrench in Green Bay's plans.

Over the course of the last several weeks, there have been rumblings that Jacobs could be suspended by the NFL. This notion gained traction last week when he was formerly charged on two counts. Jacobs was handed down a charge for battery and another for destruction of property. Both of these are misdemeanors.

On Sunday, the day that every NFL team had to trim their rosters from 90 to 53, Roger Goddell decided to place Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list. While on this list, the Packers running back will continue to collect a paycheck. However, he will not be allowed to practice with the team, play in games, or even step foot in Green Bay football facilities.

Rob Demovsky of ESPN shared the following interpretation of what the collective bargaining agreement says regarding players on the commissioner exempt list:

If my understanding of this is correct, time spent on the commissioner exempt list counts toward a future suspension.

Say if in Week 4, the NFL announces a 6-game suspension for Josh Jacobs, he would only miss 3 more games (but loses 6 games of $).

As one can see, the number of games Jacobs spends on the exempt list will count towards the number of games he is potentially suspended. If he is indeed suspended, he will have to forfeit salary to make up for the number of games it is for.

In other words, say he is on the exempt list for the first three games and then is handed a six-game suspension. He would only miss three more games and would not be paid for those games. However, he also will have to forfeit his salary for the first three games.

With Jacobs out, Marshawn Lloyd will be the starting running back in Green Bay. Kaleb Johnson was acquired via trade amid the news from the NFL and will likely serve as the backup. Chris Brooks, who signed a two-year contract earlier this year, will be the third running back on the roster.

title: Packers trade for RB Kaleb Johnson at cutdown deadline
description: Kaleb Johnson was the 83rd overall pick in the 2025 draft
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers have added depth to their running back room on Sunday, as they've traded for former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. Johnson, a 23-year-old, was a third-round pick for the Steelers coming out of Iowa last season.

Johnson ended up buried on Pittsburgh's dept chart, though, following the team's signings of Rico Dowdle and Travis Homer behind starter Jaylen Warren. As a rookie, the former All-American carried the ball just 28 times for 69 yards (2.5 yards per attempt) in the regular season, good for the third-most attempts on the team behind Warren and Kenneth Gainwell.

Funny enough, he was actually fourth on the Steelers in rushing yards last year, as tight end Jonnu Smith had nine carries for 70 yards and a touchdown. Smith, who previously played for head coach Matt LaFleur when LaFleur was an offensive coordinator for the Tennessee Titans, was signed by the Packers earlier this week.

Johnson played 11 snaps of special teams in 10 games, with 8 of those snaps being kickoff returns on which he got his hands on the ball. It doesn't seem like he has much of a background on teams other than as a kickoff returner, something that will probably go to receivers Skyy Moore and Savion Williams during the regular season. He had a long of 29 yards on his eight returns last year.

The Packers have released running back Pierre Strong Jr., according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Tom Silverstein. It looks as though Green Bay will enter the regular season with four backs on its roster: Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Johnson.

So far, there have been no reports on the compensation that the Steelers will receive for Johnson, be it a player or draft pick.

Update: NFL insider Adam Caplan is now reporting that the expected compensation for the Johnson trade is a future sixth-round pick.

#Packers are giving a 2028 sixth-round pick to the #Steelers for running back Kaleb Johnson, according to a source. The pick is their own and not the one they obtained from Miami.

So, the Packers functionally traded QB Kyle McCord for RB Kaleb Johnson.

It’s a 7th for Kaleb Johnson. Not a 6th. Even better! pic.twitter.com/iBp4Yat0Id

It is actually a seventh-round pick that was given up in the trade, not a sixth-round pick. This is interesting, since both the Packers and Steelers claimed it was a sixth-round pick, not a seventh-round pick. It's possible this is an error on the league's part.

title: Iowa State volleyball goes 2-1 at Cyclone Invitational
description: The Iowa State volleyball team experienced a rollercoaster of emotions during its season-opening tournament at Hilton Coliseum, finishing the three-day event with a pair of wins. fullText:
The Iowa State volleyball team experienced a rollercoaster of emotions during its season-opening tournament at Hilton Coliseum, finishing the three-day event with a pair of wins.

After kicking off the campaign with a dominant sweep of Loyola Chicago on Friday, the Cyclones stumbled in straight sets against Georgia Tech on Saturday, before bouncing back Sunday with a thrilling, marathon four-set victory over in-state rival the University of Northern Iowa.

The Cyclones opened their 2026 campaign in style on Friday evening, dispatching Loyola Chicago in a swift 3-0 sweep (25-12, 25-20, 25-22) in front of 2,216 fans.

Iowa State's offense was highly efficient, registering a .277 hitting percentage with 40 kills and only 14 attack errors on 94 attempts. Nayeli Ti'a paced the Cyclones with a match-high 10 kills while hitting .333 and adding nine digs. Lilly Wachholz was equally effective, contributing nine kills on .300 hitting alongside five block assists. The Cyclones' defense, anchored by Rachel Van Gorp's 13 digs and Daaliyah Kemp's six total blocks (one solo, five assists), held the Ramblers to a meager .117 hitting percentage. Setter Ava Martin orchestrated the Iowa State offense beautifully, recording 33 assists, four digs, and two service aces.

Loyola Chicago (0-1) struggled to find its footing offensively, committing 18 errors on 94 total attacks. Leyna Nguyen led the Ramblers with nine kills but was plagued by five errors. Mallory Bohl was a bright spot for Loyola, slamming seven kills with just one error for an impressive .462 hitting clip. Setter Emma Henry dished out 13 assists in two sets of action, while Jae Fitting anchored the Ramblers' back row with nine digs.

On Saturday, the Cyclones faced a tougher challenge in Georgia Tech and were swept on their home court, falling 3-0 (25-23, 25-20, 25-17) before a crowd of 2,603.

The Yellow Jackets (2-0) showcased superior defensive pressure and offensive efficiency, hitting .229 as a team with 40 kills and 16 errors. Laura Perugini Bieleski was unstoppable for Georgia Tech, racking up 15 kills on a stellar .452 hitting percentage, while also adding six digs and two blocks. Alida Bennour added eight kills and two service aces, while Zoe Humphrey controlled the net with seven kills and five block assists. Heloise Soares guided the Yellow Jacket attack with 32 assists and eight digs, while libero Mana Kaneko tallied 11 digs.

Iowa State (1-1) was plagued by errors, hitting a dismal .093 as a team with 33 kills and 23 errors on 108 attempts. Nayeli Ti'a was the lone Cyclone to reach double-digit kills with 12, but she committed seven errors on 32 swings. Daaliyah Kemp had six kills on .385 hitting, and Macie Lupkes added four kills with a highly efficient .667 percentage. Ava Martin finished with 28 assists and five digs, while Rachel Van Gorp collected 11 digs.

The Cyclones closed out the tournament on Sunday with a classic battle against UNI, emerging victorious 3-1 (25-18, 25-18, 21-25, 36-34) in front of an energetic crowd of 3,207.

After cruising through the first two sets, the Cyclones dropped the third and were pushed to the absolute limit in an epic fourth set. The marathon frame featured 20 tie scores and seven lead changes before Iowa State finally secured the match with an extraordinary 36-34 set victory.

Iowa State's offense was firing on all cylinders, hitting .324 as a team with 66 kills on 142 total attacks. Nayeli Gonzalez was sensational in her season debut, carrying the Cyclones with 26 kills on a blistering .408 hitting clip, while adding eight digs and three block assists. Nayeli Ti'a delivered another powerhouse performance, registering 22 kills on .349 hitting with two aces.

Ava Martin posted a stellar double-double, dishing out a match-high 54 assists and digging up 10 balls. Rachel Van Gorp was a defensive wall, compiling a weekend-high 27 digs and adding two service aces. At the net, Lilly Wachholz added seven kills and five blocks, while Macie Lupkes led the blocking effort with seven block assists.

UNI (1-2) put up a fierce fight, led by an extraordinary performance from Cassidy Hartman. Hartman carried the Panthers with a match-high 27 kills on 69 swings, adding 10 digs and two service aces for a total of 30 points. Isabelle Elliott added eight kills, and Claire Munch chipped in seven. Setter Reese Booth finished with a double-double, registering 37 assists and 11 digs, while Jadyn Petersen led the Panthers' defense with 18 digs.

title: Steelers Make Eye-Opening Joey Porter Jr. Decision Amid Contract Standoff
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers made a big move involving star cornerback Joey Porter Jr., as the two sides remain in a standoff when it comes to their contract extension negotiations. The post Steelers Make Eye-Opening Joey Porter Jr. Decision Amid Contract Standoff appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have trimmed their roster down to 53 players ahead of the 2026 campaign, the final step standing between them and the start of the regular season. There were some surprising decisions as part of the team's roster cuts, but for the most part, the Steelers are riding into the new year with the crop of players that many folks were expecting them to have at their disposal.

One guy who wasn't exactly on the roster bubble, but whose status was still up in the air, was star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Amid ongoing contract negotiations, Porter spent most of training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a back injury. While no new deal has been reached here, that didn't stop Pittsburgh from making a move involving Porter on Sunday.

While the Steelers actually selected Porter with the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, he was actually the first selection in the second round of the draft. That didn't figure to be much of an issue at the time, but it has actually played a surprising role in Porter's ongoing contract negotiations with Pittsburgh.

Since he wasn't a first-round pick, that means Porter's rookie contract didn't come with a fifth-year option, which the front office would have obviously exercised this offseason. Instead, Porter is entering the final year of his rookie deal, and he hasn't been shy in expressing his desire to receive a contract extension. The Steelers have been open to giving Porter a new deal, but there is a wide gap between the two sides in terms of his compensation.

As a result of these ongoing negotiations, Porter landed on the PUP list with a back injury, with some folks simply believing he wouldn't have practiced regardless due to his contract situation. If that was the case, it was a shrewd move to open up another roster spot, but now that the regular season is here, Pittsburgh needs Porter on the field. Even with his contract saga still hovering over the team, the Steelers have activated Porter off the PUP list ahead of the start of the regular season.

Activated off Active/Physically Unable to Perform: DB Joey Porter Jr.," the Steelers announced on their official website.

Porter has been a star corner for the Steelers since entering the pros, which is why settling his contract situation is so important. Last season, Porter racked up 52 tackles, 14 pass breakups, and one sack in 14 games of action, all of which were starts. Even though he didn't practice at all during training camp, Pittsburgh is counting on Porter to open the season as their top cornerback.

Whether or not he will be ready to go by the time Week 1 rolls around, though, is still unknown. While his back injury isn't expected to hold him out for four games (which is what would have happened had he stayed on the PUP list), there's no guarantee he can get himself up to speed in time for the season opener. Porter getting activated to the active roster is a big move, but his status still bears watching over the next couple of weeks.

title: Winnipeg Jets Must Consider Major Factor in Connor Hellebuyck Trade
description: Unless interest in the Eastern Conference collapses, it's clear the Jets must complete a Connor Hellebuyck trade with a team that won't keep them out of a potential playoff competition next season. The post Winnipeg Jets Must Consider Major Factor in Connor Hellebuyck Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It's now painfully obvious that Connor Hellebuyck won't finish his career in Winnipeg. The likely future Hall of Fame goaltender has a full No Movement Clause in his contract, but that won't stop a Connor Hellebuyck trade from coming to fruition. In fact, multiple teams likely can begin looking at trade packages. As Chris Johnston of TSN and The Athletic notes, the Jets netminder has shown greater willingness to waive his trade protection than other notable trade-minded stars.

There are other factors, however, that will slow it down. According to Johnston, return is the primary factor. There's likely another one hidden and lurking. Preventing a Connor Hellebuyck trade from coming to fruition is the state of the Jets both on and off the ice.

One key difference with the Connor Hellebuyck trade request compared to others around the NHL is that he’s willing to waive his NMC for a variety of teams.

The offers haven’t been to Winnipeg’s liking just yet, obviously, but they’re not totally handcuffed.

— Chris Johnston (@reporterchris) August 28, 2026

https://platform.x.com/widgets.js

This isn't just about winning the trade on value. Winnipeg has to figure out how far back a Hellebuyck trade will set them.

At the time, Buffalo Sabres ownership reportedly had no interest in sending Eichel to the New York Rangers. The Sabres intended to basically charge the Rangers extra for Eichel, seemingly concerned about the optics of the franchise player winning with the 'big brother' of the tri-state area.

Now, the factors at play here are slightly different. First, the Jets are not in a clear-cut rebuild like Buffalo was at the time. Second, Winnipeg isn't purely worried about the optics. That's the critical point here. The Jets need to win this trade because the future of pro hockey in Winnipeg is riding on it. In the past few years, the Jets' ownership structure has publicly acknowledged some concerns. The Athletic reported in 2024 that the Jets were 'sounding the alarm' on their attendance concerns.

Surprisingly, those concerns emerged in the midst of a 110-point season. The next season, the Jets won the Presidents' Trophy in a 116-point season in 2025-26. They also won a playoff round, though Jets fans likely imagined they'd have advanced deeper that year. It's not clear if that fully allayed ownership's concerns. Still, the Jets did see a year-over-year boost in tickets reported in 2025.

Then last year happened, and the Jets collapsed. For the second time in five seasons, the Jets were basically non-competitive following multiple playoff berths. This failure was even more alarming, considering the 34-point year-over-year drop for a franchise that already has the second-smallest capacity of any NHL arena. That failure, which saw the Jets struggle almost everywhere, has directly led to a potential Connor Hellebuyck trade.

So now the Jets have to ask a simple question: can they take the best deal available? Conversely, is it more important to get Hellebuyck out of the Western Conference so they don't have to directly compete against him? This is less about optics and more about something hockey fans might have some sympathy for — figuring out how to compete for a playoff spot while simultaneously making the team worse and a Western Conference foe better.

Carolina, New Jersey, Pittsburgh, Washington, Buffalo, Detroit, Florida, Montreal, Ottawa and Toronto all have good reasons to explore a Connor Hellebuyck trade. That doesn't mean that all of them could pull off a potential deal. Toronto, Ottawa and Florida all recently committed to big-money goaltenders. The former two would likely want to move their respective netminders. Both Sergei Bobrovsky and Linus Ullmark have full No Movement Clauses. Florida has more flexibility, but the Panthers have few assets remaining to win a bidding war.

Montreal, Detroit and Buffalo all have good reason to get interested. These are teams with big prospect pipelines and the ability to send a goalie back the other way in a potential trade. While the Habs just committed to a Jakub Dobes contract extension, it has not kicked in yet. They could pair Hellebuyck with Jacob Fowler, one of the best goaltending prospects on the planet. Detroit could also have interest if such a move could be used to convince Dylan Larkin to rescind his trade request. The Sabres' interest is obvious, particularly after poor goaltending ended their first playoff run in 15 years.

The Metropolitan Division is murkier. Washington, clearly all-in on their own last dance with Alex Ovechkin, could be enticed to get involved. It would be complicated with the Capitals' salary cap situation. Carolina let Freddie Andersen walk, but it's hard to know if they'd increase their offer from earlier this summer. New Jersey's three-goalie tandem doesn't look ideal. However, there would be numerous other factors at play for New Jersey, including the status of Quinn Hughes. Kyle Dubas appears interested in bringing a big star to Pittsburgh. That said, Hellebuyck, 33, might be a little on the older side for them.

If there's enough interest out east, this won't matter. Still, it's plausible that no one in the Eastern Conference might step up for a Connor Hellebuyck trade. In the meantime, the list of suitors out west could include everyone but Vancouver, Calgary, Nashville and Dallas. Now, that doesn't mean they can all do it. For some teams, the interest is likely going to be soft. St. Louis might inquire about the price, but Joel Hofer might be a potential rising star. As a result, the Blues wouldn't be motivated. Anaheim, similarly, isn't likely to be very motivated, particularly while the cap situation there is a problem.

Colorado could build a trade around Mackenzie Blackwood but not much else. Similarly, Minnesota is already asset-depleted following the Quinn Hughes trade. Sure, they could build something around one of their two goaltenders, but it likely won't be enough. Los Angeles, Edmonton and Vegas are likely all interested and motivated. None of them likely have the goods to make such a move.

Chicago, Utah, San Jose and Seattle are likely the four best fits. Two of those teams will play Winnipeg four times per season, and the other two will play them three times per season. The Jets would directly compete for a playoff spot against Utah and Chicago in the Central, while simultaneously looking at wildcard spots against the other two.

The Jets are not rebuilding. It's not clear, even if ownership were to sign off on a rebuild, that it would be their best path forward. The Central Division is difficult, certainly. Still, there's volatility in Minnesota as long as the Quinn Hughes situation lingers. Utah looks poised to take a big step and join the division's big boys like Colorado and Dallas. Admittedly, those two might both have taken a step back this offseason. St. Louis has potential. However, the Blues have lacked consistency.

That does leave a path for Winnipeg to at least be competitive in the division, ideally still able to draw fans in as a result. Unless interest in the Eastern Conference collapses, it's clear the Jets must complete a Connor Hellebuyck trade with a team that won't keep them out of a potential playoff competition next season.

title: NFL Cutdowns: Former Packers pre-draft visitors released on Sunday
description: The Panthers waived linebacker Trevin Wallace, who was a starter for them last year, on Sunday
fullText:
I'll keep this one short: The Green Bay Packers target their pre-draft visitors at a high clip, whether it's the draft, as initial undrafted free agents or further down the line. For example, last cutdown cycle the team traded a pick for offensive linemen Darian Kinnard and picked up tight end Josh Whyle to the practice squad. Whyle eventually ended up winning a roster spot and made this year's initial 53-man roster.

So, who was just made available to the Packers? Good question. So far, these are the players who just hit the market and were brought to Green Bay during their draft cycle (since 2022, when the team started targeting more draft picks).

Can I interest anyone in Sean Clifford as a QB3 again?

The one I'm most interested here is rookie Damon Bankston, who received eight times the guarantees to sign with the New York Giants than the Packers' UDFA signing Jaden Nixon got this cycle. If Green Bay is pivoting to a more outside zone-based scheme, which has been the indication, I think Bankston fits really well. With that being said, he would probably be a practice squad signing immediately, not a 53-man roster guy.

I don't think the team wants to go down the Samori Toure path again, but rookie receiver Anthony Smith is interesting. Smith was taken two picks after Packers kicker Trey Smack. The seventh-round pick did not make it on the Dallas Cowboys' roster. He ran a 4.45-second 40-yard dash at 6'2" and 197 pounds.

Both Kiran Amegadjie and Esa Pole are players I could see the Packers adding to the bottom of their offensive line unit. Amegadjie was a third-round pick out of Yale for the Chicago Bears back in 2024, but he never caught on with the team. Esa Pola is a second-year former UDFA who was working with the first-team unit as the team's left tackle in Kansas City at points this summer, but the Chiefs traded for Diego Pounds right before the cutdown deadline.

With seven interior defensive linemen on the 53-man roster, I'm not sure the Packers even need a practice squad defensive lineman right now.

Sam Williams was arrested for felony sexual battery at Ole Miss, but the charges were later dropped. I know now this isn't a great time to say this, but the Packers bring in a lot of prospects with "off-field" red flags for visits, and they generally do it to rule them out completely. I do not expect Williams to be on Green Bay's short list.

Here's an interesting one: Trevin Wallace, the 2024 third-rounder who made 12 starts in 12 games played last year for the Carolina Panthers, was waived by the Panthers today. In total, he played 25 games (20 starts) for Carolina over two regular seasons. I could see the team taking a swing on him.

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister, Chiefs

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister actually started his college career off as a fairly big recruit, but wound up bouncing around schools after two years at TCU. He ended up at New Mexico, UT-Chattanooga and Louisiana-Monroe after that. He was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs, and it's not like the Packers' third-team defensive backs played well in the preseason. Maybe they change things up.

Safety is a position that will probably be more impacted on the practice squad level, if anything, than on the 53-man roster level, but two were made available today. Chris Edmonds has played almost exclusively as a special teamer when he's been active in NFL games in his career, while Jammie Robinson, a former fifth-round pick, is looking to catch on with his sixth team in four years. He's been available before, and the Packers haven't added him, so I'm not sure the 25-year-old is going to be a priority for them now.

fullText:
Throughout training camp and the preseason, the Detroit Lions have been without safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles), who both remained on the PUP list.

Now, with the regular season approaching, the Lions have provided a clearer outlook on the status of both players.

According to the Lions, Joseph and Branch will begin the season on the PUP list, meaning both will miss at least the first four games of the 2026 campaign.

Last season, Joseph and Branch combined to miss 15 games last season due to injuries. Joseph was sidelined by a lower-body issue that ultimately ended his season after Week 6, while Branch suffered a torn Achilles against the Dallas Cowboys in December that also brought his season to an early close.

Earlier this month at the start of Training Camp, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that Joseph was progressing in his rehab but was on a similar timeline to that of Branch, hinting that expected both players to miss the start of the season.

"Well, Kerby right now, first of all, he's dealing with a personal issue," Campbell said. "But, his rehab is coming along very well. OK, so I still see him on the (Brian) Branch plan if that makes sense. And Branch is doing well, too. So, those guys, we're talking about on down the road, the season's already begun, but I like where Kerby's at."

Not long after the 2026 NFL Draft in which the Lions did not select a safety, general manager Brad Holmes offered a somewhat optimistic health outlook for both Joseph and Branch.

"It wasn't that we intentionally didn't draft a safety because we feel good about them (Joseph and Branch). I feel like they're both trending in the right direction, but it just didn't line up," Holmes said. "Just like it hasn't lined up at other positions in the past, we didn't ignore it. There were some good ones that were out there that just got picked before we were able to, but it just didn't quite line up. I didn't really think that class was as deep either, so it had to line up and you had to strike right."

"I think that you talk about a guy like Cam and you've got to look at it like, 'If this guy went back into school, where would he be a year from now?" Eagles general manager Howie Roseman said after the 2025 NFL Draft. "Where can we get this guy two years from now? What would that look like?'"

Williams slipped to Day 3 of the 2025 draft, but he was considered a Day 2 talent who needed to clean up consistency issues.

title: 9 winners and 4 losers from the initial Bengals 53-man roster
description: Here are some winners and losers when it comes to the first version of the Bengals’ final roster.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals have made their cuts and released the first version of their final roster on Sunday. They cut down from around 90 players to the 53 that will hopefully win the Bengals their first Super Bowl.

Of course, the Bengals will take a look at who was cut by the other 31 teams, and odds are they could put in a waiver claim or two. Until that happens, though, here are some winners and losers from the Bengals' initial 53-man roster.

There might not be a cooler story this season than Meyers'. From getting no D1 offers out of high school and having to pay $100 to try out for a CFL team to making a 53-man roster at 26 years old is the kind of stuff they make movies about. Meyers earned his spot too, catching 11 passes on 13 targets for 121 yards. He led the team in receptions and receiving yards this preseason, and will now take his spot on the most talented wide receiver corps in the NFL.

You know those guys that you can't help but like? You know, the ones that usually play for other teams that you always think, "Man, I wish that guy was a Bengal." Robinson is officially that guy. The seventh-round pick had a multi-sack preseason and not only made the Bengals' initial 53-man roster, but he appears primed to get some playing time early.

Stewart is a winner because, despite a nasty-looking hyperextension of his knee at the start of training camp, he won't be joining Brian Parker II and Ja'Sir Taylor on IR. That doesn't mean he's going to be ready to go by Week 1 (though it's not out of the realm of possibility), but it means he 'should' be good to go before Week 5, when he would have been eligible to come off IR.

Though Newton looked solid on Friday night against the Eagles in the Bengals' third preseason game, he struggled through much of camp and was reportedly in the doghouse. It appeared as if he was on route to getting cut, but thanks to Ja'Sir Taylor being placed on IR (with designation to return) due to a hamstring injury. This opened the door for Newton to stick around.

For now. These next four weeks are crucial for Newton's chances of remaining on the roster. Play well, and he may very well remain there for the rest of 2026.

The Bengals' starting offensive line is set, and has been set since before the offseason even began. Rivers is one of four backup offensive linemen to make the first version of the Bengals' final roster, but he wouldn't be if it weren't for the fact that Brian Parker II got placed on IR with Taylor with a knee injury.

Maybe the Bengals find a new offensive lineman from the many that are being cut throughout the league, but for now Rivers is on the roster.

This was likely the biggest surprise addition to the Bengals' 53-man roster. I would have thought Charlie Jones or Mitchell Tinsley would have the inside spot, but it was Williams who is the team's WR6 and likely kick and punt returner.

PFF gave him a score of 65.0 for kick returning and a 62.8 for punt returning compared to Jones' 67.5 and 69.8, but he also caught seven passes to Jones' four and Tinsley's three.

Brooks, the team's third running back, didn't do a lot to inspire confidence that, if the Bengals were to lean on him, he would be able to move the ball down the field. He only averaged 3.8 yards per carry on his 13 total rushing attempts.

Kentrel Bullock and Jamal Haynes never really had much of a chance at cracking the 53-man roster, but it wasn't for lack of trying. They both averaged more yards per carry, and both looked pretty solid on Friday night in Philly.

That, and the Bengals were reportedly interested in Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. But once Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list, the Packers got desperate enough to trade for Johnson.

So for the time being, Brooks doesn't have any real competition for his spot.

Speaking of a lack of competition…

Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter

Knight and Carter continue to have a stranglehold on their jobs after the Bengals opted to keep just two other linebackers on the roster in Oren Burks and Swayze Bozeman, neither of whom looks capable of pushing for a starting spot.

Unless the Bengals make a trade or sign someone like Bobby Wagner, Knight and Carter are the starting linebackers for the foreseeable future. Let's hope they're ready to make a big jump from last year.

Jones and Tinsley were on the outside looking in when all was said and done on Sunday. Jones, a fourth-round pick in 2023, has been a solid return specialist in his time in Cincinnati, and Tinsley was one of the fun and exciting stories of the 2025 season.

Unfortunately, they were outshone by the trio of Williams, Colbie Young, and Meyers.

Taylor is on IR, but that's not why he's on the losers list. He's on this list because the four weeks he'll miss could be the four weeks Newton needs to prove he does belong on the final roster and hold on to his spot — whether that be on the field on defense or on special teams.

Taylor was signed in free agency on a one-year deal, and he was placed on IR with a designation to return. That return, at the earliest, would be in Week 5.

Newton, on the other hand, is a former fifth-round draft pick of the Bengals who is under contract through 2027. In other words, there's more incentive for the front office to keep Newton if this is a close battle.

Jackson struggled to get on the field in 2025, but the additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen really sealed his fate. Now that fate is official. The 2024 third-round pick is now going to the practice squad or will be playing elsewhere.

The 2026 Florida State Seminoles are in an intriguing position. After a pair of seasons missing the College Football Playoff, they are looking to get back to the success they had a few years ago. "Playing SMU and then in Tuscaloosa and then home for Virginia and then at Louisville, at Miami, and Clemson by Halloween is a recipe for disaster."

After a pair of bad seasons with a combined record of 7-17, Seminoles coach Mike Norvell cannot afford to be out of the College Football Playoff picture that early into the season. title: Bruins’ McAvoy, Swayman Land Side-by-Side in NHL’s Top 50
description: Charlie McAvoy and Jeremy Swayman are among the best at their positions, and the NHL Network has them side-by-side in […]
fullText:
Charlie McAvoy and Jeremy Swayman are among the best at their positions, and the NHL Network has them side-by-side in its league-wide rankings.

On Sunday night, the NHL Network revealed the first 10 names on its Top 50 Players Right Now list, starting with No. 50 and finishing with No. 41. Two Boston Bruins landed on the first part of the list, with Jeremy Swayman ranked 42nd and Charlie McAvoy in front of him at No. 41.

Olympic gold medalist Charlie McAvoy is #️⃣4️⃣1️⃣ on NHL Network's Top 50 Players Right Now list!

📺: #NHLTopPlayers on NHL Network pic.twitter.com/GQZDxwNOWd

McAvoy, who ranked No. 38 in last year's list, fell back three spots after posting career highs in assists (50) and points (61). His slight drop did not lead to much criticism from NHL Network analysts Tony Luftman, Mike Rupp, and Mike Johnson, who were full of praise for McAvoy during Sunday night's reveal show.

"He's so unique because he does everything well. He does everything well, and some of the things that some players do well, like, I don't know, get 50 assists as a defenseman, generally aren't physically imposing. He is," Rupp said. "What do you need? He plays through injuries; we've seen that. He's nuts. The absolute warrior that he is."

"The only thing, for me, that from watching Charlie McAvoy, sometimes gets him in trouble, [is] because he cares too much," Rupp added. "Sometimes he tries to do a little bit too much. When he just goes and plays his game, he is a difference maker."

Even if Rupp believes McAvoy tries to do too much, he does everything for the Bruins. He averaged 24:23 of ice time per night last season, and he has led the Bruins in that category in seven of the last eight seasons. There has never been a year where McAvoy has averaged less than 22 minutes of ice time per night. He also punches in minutes on both the power play and penalty kill, and finished the 2025-26 season with a career-high 23 power play points (2-21–23).

"Underrated offensively. You think about Charlie McAvoy, I think people's first thought goes to all the stuff. The physical play, the defense, the leadership, the emotion, all that stuff," Mike Johnson said. "You're like, wait a second, 50 assists? That's a big, big number for a defenseman."

"He does it all for the Boston Bruins, and he also seems to represent the next person in the line of leadership, who the Boston Bruins want to be as a club […] He's the guy who plays hard, he's physical, he's in your face, he's the kind of player that the Bruins fans want to get behind and the Bruins organization wants to represent them."

There may not be one specific part of McAvoy's game that defines him, and Mike Johnson believes that's exactly what separates him from other defensemen in the league.

"If you want to talk about the best all-around guys, who can bring it [on] both ends, he's one of the best in the world."

Also Read:After Career-High Season, Charlie McAvoy Still Ranks 11th Among NHL Defensemen

Jeremy Swayman (@NHLBruins) is the first goaltender to appear on this year's Top 50 Players Right Now list!

📺: #NHLTopPlayers on NHL Network pic.twitter.com/6eYSYU2MR5

Jeremy Swayman did not rank in the top 50 last season, but landed at No. 49 entering the 2024-25 season. He's back on the list after a bounce-back season, and he was the first goaltender revealed in the top 50.

Swayman finished the year with 31 wins, topping his previous career-high of 25. He posted a .908 save percentage and a 2.71 goals against average, but he led the league in games started with a save percentage above .900 with 38. His third-place finish in Vezina Trophy voting only hints at how impactful he was to the Bruins last season, and how much of a role he played in helping the black and gold get back into the postseason.

"[The Bruins] were really driven by their great goalie. And Jeremy Swayman, you can talk about the goals saved above expected; you look at the traditional numbers here, [shows] how impactful he was on their team's success," NHL Network analyst Mike Johnson said. "This is what a great goalie can do. They can take an average team and make them an above-average team, and that's really what he did last year for Boston."

According to MoneyPuck, Swayman finished with 28.8 goals saved above expected, second to Washington's Logan Thompson. That marked a 37.9-goal improvement from the 2024-25 season, when he finished with a minus-9.1 GSAx.

"When you're talking about goals saved above expected, generally speaking, since we started tracking this, it comes from teams that don't really defend well, because that shows that the goaltenders are seeing stuff they probably shouldn't see," Mike Rupp said on the reveal show. "It's not always that case, but when you see this situation, Boston, if they can't improve the defensive game, get a little more predictable, he's shown that he could be a difference maker."

Just two weeks ago, the NHL ranked Swayman as the fifth-best goaltender in the league right now. Mike Rupp went on to call the position "one of the hardest, most polarizing positions in all of sports," and continued, saying that remaining consistent year over year is one of the toughest things to do as a goaltender.

title: Rutgers Finds Its Goals, Then Watches a Two-Goal Lead Disappear in 3-3 Draw With Providence
description: The Scarlet Knights scored twice in the opening 19 minutes and led by two with half an hour to play. Providence answered with three, the last two in 69 seconds.
fullText:
PISCATAWAY, N.J. — Seventeen days and three states after it opened the season in Knoxville, and three days after the weather took its home opener, Rutgers finally played a home game, and the goal drought that followed it up the coast ended barely two minutes in, but the clean sheet streak also ended in gutwrenching fashion. Providence drew Rutgers 3-3 on Sunday night at Yurcak Field, with the last two goals coming in the final minutes of the game.

Rutgers arrived at 0-1-2 with two clean sheets and 180 scoreless minutes behind it. Olivia Bodmer made six saves in the 0-0 draw at UConn and kept a second consecutive shutout at Fairfield, where Rutgers took the larger share of the shots and put too few of them on frame. The last Scarlet Knights goal came from Emma Johns in the 76th minute at Tennessee on Aug. 13, 17 days ago. With three goals in the game, Rutgers scored more than their previous three games combined, invoking a newfound hope in the attack.

Providence came to Piscataway unbeaten at 2-0-3, with three draws in five matches. The Friars opened 1-1 against UMass Lowell, beat Rhode Island 3-0, drew Monmouth, played out a scoreless 90 minutes at Northeastern and beat Stonehill 2-1 on Thursday. Freshman Jocy Koffi scored in each of the first two matches, including an 87th-minute equalizer against Lowell, and took BIG EAST Rookie of the Week; junior defender Stephanie Schoeley was named Defensive Player of the Week the same day. They went 6-6-4 last season, 3-4-3 in the Big East, and was picked sixth in the conference preseason coaches' poll. This clearly showed given their fight near the end of the game

GK: Olivia Bodmer
D: Julia Joseph, Morgan Hippeli, Lindsey Hailey, Jayme Malanda
M: Gabriela Gil, Lily Ann Phillips
F: Lilia Calvert, Reilly McGlinn, Ashley Baran, Amanda Thornton
Subs: Tommi Valente, Olivia Russomanno, Marian Dunne, Emma Johns, Sophia Stiles, Audrey Cain, Madelyn O'Neill, Riley Morris, Bea Tinoco

Mike O'Neill made one change to the XI that started at Fairfield, and it came in the back four. Jayme Malanda, who did not appear in the Fairfield box score at all, started at Providence. Patricia Tsokos, who had started each of the first three matches, does not appear in this one, not in the XI, not among the nine substitutes, no minutes logged.

That is now three consecutive weeks in which a Rutgers player has moved in or out of the matchday squad without explanation. Everything else held: Bodmer in goal, Gil and Phillips paired centrally, Calvert and Thornton keeping their places up front for a fourth straight start.

O'Neill used nine substitutes for a fourth straight match, and again emptied the bench before halftime. Then he did something he had not done all season, he put the entire starting XI back on the field for the second half. All eleven who kicked off restarted the match.

Gabriela Gil found Ashley Baran at 1:43 and Rutgers led before Providence had settled into the match at all. Amanda Thornton nearly doubled it 27 seconds later, dragging a shot right of the frame, and for a moment it looked like the kind of opening that decides a game early.

Providence did not let it. Signe Tingager forced Bodmer into a save at 2:46, Hinkle did the same 18 seconds later, and the Friars won corners at 3:11 and 6:16 as Rutgers spent the first ten minutes defending its own box. Hinkle struck the woodwork at 9:58. Meg Roden made Bodmer work again at 11:09. Tingager tested her a second time at 17:50, low to the left. Providence was chasing the game and playing like it, and the pressure produced real chances rather than territory.

Rutgers helped them along. Bodmer misplayed one save that the Friars could not punish, and a loose Calvert pass out of the back handed Providence a look it did not finish. Neither mistake cost anything, but both were the kind that have cost this team before. Then Calvert delivered for Reilly McGlinn at 18:28, and Rutgers led 2-0 against the run of play as it looked from the stands.

The numbers say otherwise. Rutgers finished the half with eight shots to Providence's seven and led 3-2 on corners. The Friars generated urgency without generating an edge in either column. What separated the teams was the frame. Providence put five of its seven attempts on target and scored none of them. Rutgers put two on target and scored both. Maria Ravotti did not make a save in 45 minutes of work.

Providence responded to the second goal immediately, sending on Marryn Gruhn and Kaitlyn Brady at 18:28, and O'Neill began his own rotation at 24:47 with Tommi Valente and Marian Dunne. Koffi drew a save at 24:14 and then the half went quiet. Dunne shot at 31:03, Morgan Hippeli at 32:57, Olivia Russomanno wide at 33:45, Lily Gibbs wide at the other end at 34:38. Rutgers was flagged offside three times before the break and Providence once. Both benches kept emptying, and by 38:04 the two teams had made 13 substitutions between them.

Caitlin Daley replaced Ravotti at the break and was tested inside ten seconds, Koffi forcing Bodmer into a save at the other end on the first attack of the half. Koffi won a corner at 48:51 and then scored from it, the ball curling in without touching anyone on its way. It was her fifth of the season and the kind of goal that changes a match's temperature.

For a while it did not. Rutgers restored the two-goal cushion at 54:31 when a Providence clearance went into the Friars' own net, and Providence answered by changing seven players at once at 56:49. That group came out pressing, Caitlin Driscoll's shot at 57:26 was blocked and credited as a team save, Koffi drew another Bodmer stop at 57:57, Courtnee Pickles and Samantha Kolb both had looks inside 70 seconds, and then the Friars stopped shooting almost entirely. From 58:32 to 74:15, Providence did not register an attempt.

That stretch belonged to Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights took 16 shots in the second half and seven corners, and for half an hour they controlled the ball in a way they have not managed at any point this season. Dunne had four attempts off the bench. Baran drew a save from Daley at 63:31 and shot over at 63:40. Lindsey Hailey forced another save at 66:33, Emma Johns another at 67:56. Calvert struck the crossbar at 81:59 with a shot that looked in from the moment it left her foot.

Daley saved all five Rutgers attempts that reached her. The only goal she conceded in 45 minutes was the one Providence scored on itself.

The discipline went first. Kolb was booked at 75:37, Leila Anazagasty-Pursoo at 78:50, and then Hippeli at 80:03, withdrawn 29 seconds later. Julia Joseph was cautioned at 85:57. All four yellow cards in the match came inside the final 15 minutes. In between the last two, Kolb delivered a ball to Hinkle at 84:51 and the Buffalo transfer scored her first goal for Providence, a finish that went to video review and stood. Koffi equalized at 86:00.

A two-goal lead Rutgers had held for half an hour was gone inside a minute and change, and the Scarlet Knights could not get it back. Hippeli's shot at 88:59 was the last thing either team generated. Rutgers outshot Providence 24-18 and led 10-4 on corners. Providence put 13 of its 18 attempts on target and Rutgers seven of 24. Koffi alone hit the frame six times in six tries. Bodmer made nine saves and conceded three. No Rutgers player registered more than two shots on goal.

The result leaves Rutgers winless with three draws and a shot profile that reads better than the record. Four matches in, the Scarlet Knights have produced their most complete half of soccer and their worst 90 seconds, and both happened Sunday.

Providence moves to 2-0-4, a team that has now drawn four of six. Rutgers gets Princeton at Yurcak on Sunday before Big Ten play opens, with the Boston College makeup still unscheduled.

The goals came back. Holding them is the next thing.

title: Eagles surprisingly waive both international rookies and risk losing them
description: Eagles waive two rookies.

The Eagles waived seventh-round pick Uar Bernard and undrafted edge rusher Joshua Weru on Sunday night.

Bernard, from Nigeria, and Weru, from Kenya, were among the best stories during training camp. They had never played football prior to this season, but the Eagles took a chance on both players, and the early results were encouraging.

Especially with Weru. He finished with a sack against the Patriots and applied pressure in the other two preseason games. He is an exceptional athlete.

Bernard, a defensive tackle, is bigger a project than Weru. He struggled at times during the games, but it's still surprising to see him get waived. He's an elite athlete with absurd physical upside.

The Eagles took a risk waiving both players. They were both expected to make Philadelphia's 53-man roster to avoid losing them to another team.

NFL teams could claim both players on Monday afternoon off the waiver wire. Weru is more likely to be claimed because he showed more upside in the games.

Bernard is 6-foot-4 and 306 pounds with a body fat of 6%. He ran the 40-yard dash at his Pro Day in 4.63 seconds. Another NFL team could be bold enough to claim him off waivers if they believe in his long-term potential.

title: New York Jets 2026 practice squad tracker with news and live updates
description: The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026. The work is not finished, however. The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week.
fullText:
The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026. The work is not finished, however.

The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week. Every week, two players can be activated from the practice squad to play in games. These players do not need to be added to the active roster the first three times they are activated for a game. The fourth time, however, the team must add them to the 53 man roster.

Practice squad players are technically free agents and able to sign with the active roster of any team aside from upcoming opponents.

Who is eligible for the practice squad?

Teams can use up to 16 of their 17 slots on players with no NFL seasons or one season (with less than nine games played) if they so choose. For a fully stocked practice squad, the minimum number of players with this level of experience is 6.

Teams are also allowed to choose up to 10 practice squad players with more experience. No more than six can have more than two years of experience in the NFL.

Finally, one spot must go to an international player.
