title: 6 stunning choices on the Lions’ initial 53-man roster
description: Here are five of the biggest shocks from the Detroit Lions’ initial 53-man roster.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions dropped their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season—see it here—and there were plenty of big surprises in their choices. Now, the Lions are likely to make some tweaks over the next 48 hours, so it's important not to overreact until they truly settle on a Week 1 roster.

But here are 6 shocking decisions the Lions front office made with this initial roster.

A few weeks ago, Dan Campbell noted that the RB4 competition between Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small was neck-and-neck. However, since then, it's been almost all Saylors. He finished the preseason with more scrimmage yards than any other player in the NFL, while Small failed to stay on the field. Small missed the first preseason game with an injury, left Game 2 with a concussion, and left Game 3 with another injury.

Yet the Lions liked enough of what they saw in Small to give him a coveted roster spot. That is perhaps the most shocking decision of all.

Not far behind was Detroit's decision to only keep four receivers. While everyone had Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, and Tay Martin on their 53-man roster predictions, a fifth almost seemed necessary and certain.

Greg Dortch is a trusted veteran who looked great as a punt returner all August and had experience with offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. When it was revealed that Dortch was being released, it was certainly Tom Kennedy who won the spot, right? Nope, he was released in the final cuts as well.

So…. what is the Lions' plan at punt returner? Just a few weeks ago, special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said the competition was between Dortch and Kennedy. So, either one (or both) is coming back to the practice squad (or 53-man roster), or some unknown player on the roster will step up. But in all honesty, I don't have the faintest of clues who on the current roster could take over those duties.

Not many questioned whether Tyler Conklin's spot on the roster was in jeopardy. He frequently repped ahead of Jackson Meeks, and looked just fine in his role as TE3 behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright. For as many two- and three-tight end formations the Lions are expected to use, having an experienced veteran like Conklin seemed like a no-brainer—especially after the struggles they went through last year when LaPorta and Wright went down with injuries.

And while many of us had Meeks on the roster as TE4, trusting him as the team's TE3 is a risky move for a player who is still learning the nuances of the position. That said, Meeks earned it on special teams, and that's where his initial role will be.

One final thing to keep in mind: as a vested veteran, Conklin's salary would have been fully guaranteed if he was on the active roster in Week 1, and this could be their way of circumventing that rule. If they add him to the practice squad, they could elevate him in Week 1, then re-sign him to the active roster in Week 2.

EDGE Eric O'Neill: 6-foot-2, 250
EDGE Ahmed Hassanein: 6-foot-2, 275
DT Skyler Gill-Howard: 6-foot, 280
DT Mekhi Wingo: 6-foot, 282

These four players who made the 53 shined in the preseason predominantly because of their pass rush, while their abilities as run defenders are still a work in progress. Meanwhile, these players:

EDGE Anthony Lucas: 6-foot-5, 265
DT Chris Smith: 6-foot-1, 310
DT Ben Stille: 6-foot-4, 296

None of them made it. This represents a pretty clear shift in the preferences of their defensive linemen, with a newfound lean into getting to the quarterback.

That isn't to say they don't have size on the roster. Alim McNeill (6-foot-2, 310), Tyleik Williams (6-foot-3, 325), Levi Onwuzurike (6-foot-3, 304), and DJ Wonnum (6-foot-5, 262) are all big for their positions. But it appears they want some juice with their reserves.

Maybe not the biggest shock, considering Rolder himself told the media that he believes he's close to a return. But when the injury happened, it appeared the Lions' fourth-round rookie was going to miss significant time. Instead, the Lions believe his development is important enough to stay on the roster and avoid a four-week absence on IR.

Detroit had enough linebacker reserves that they would've been fine if Rolder went on IR, but they clearly believe in Rolder's health and ability to make a difference early this season.

Through a few weeks of training camp, there was no better story than Nick Whiteside. He had worked his way up from the bottom of the depth chart to sharing some first-team defense reps at cornerback. He played a physical style of game that seemed like a great fit.

And while he admittedly cooled down a bit toward the end of training camp, some of that was simply due to him having to cover the safety position that was plagued by injuries. I thought flashing that versatility would only strengthen his case for the 53-man roster. Instead, Detroit favored guys like Ennis Rakestraw, who has more potential, and Khalil Dorsey, who is one of the team's best special teamers.

title: Scottie Scheffler ends the longest run in PGA Tour's money game
description: Tiger Woods had been the PGA Tour's all-time earnings leader since 2000. Scottie Scheffler's Tour Championship win put him past the golf legend.
fullText:
Tiger Woods was 24 and going for his seventh straight win when he tied for second at Torrey Pines. The check was $264,000. It made him the PGA Tour's all-time money leader, which nobody really thought much about at the time. It was Feb. 13, 2000.

He never moved from atop that list. Even through the swing changes, the surgeries and the years he barely played at all.

Woods was the all-time earnings leader for over 26 years, until Sunday.

Scottie Scheffler took that title from him Sunday afternoon in Atlanta. It took him less than a decade.

Scheffler began the final round of the Tour Championship three shots behind, but passed Viktor Hovland on the back nine and won his second FedEx Cup. The win was worth $10 million and it moved him to $130,390,661 for his career. Woods sits at $120, 999,166.

Nobody is saying their careers are close.

Woods won 82 times and took 15 majors. Scheffler is 30 with 22 wins and four majors. But times have changed. Woods beat Davis Love III in a playoff in Las Vegas in 1996 for his first Tour title and he got a check worth $297,000. The man who finished last at East Lake on Sunday made $355,000.

But Woods took to social media to congratulate Scheffler on his 2026 season.

"Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No. 1. Those are some numbers to be proud of. Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie," Woods wrote on X.com.

title: Another player involved in college eligibility suit gets cut by an NFL team
description: Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.  Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53.
fullText:
Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.

Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53. He could now try to get a fifth year of eligibility if he is not claimed on waivers by another team Monday. He'll become a free agent if he's not picked up and is among the players granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court earlier this month that would make them eligible to return to college athletics. Pyburn's likely landing spot would be LSU.

Four other players who spent time on NFL rosters this offseason before being cut were also part of the case: former LSU running back TJ Harden, former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson.

These players all entered the NFL draft process because they had used up their four years of eligibility. The NCAA announced a rule change in June allowing players who began college in 2023 or later to have five years to play five seasons.

That rule didn't apply to these players because they entered college in 2022. They have sued the NCAA, arguing they're being deprived of education and potential name, image and likeness benefits by being excluded from the rule.

The Power Four conferences have all ruled that players who signed NFL contracts are ineligible to return to college, but those rules remain in legal limbo until court cases are resolved. The Southeastern Conference's rule is part of a court hearing scheduled for Thursday. SEC rosters become final Friday.

Under NFL rules, any player who returns to college for any time will be ineligible to play this season. Those players would become free agents who are free to sign with any team in 2027.

Here's a look at some of the players who spent time in NFL camps this summer and now might return to college:

Pyburn originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Tampa Bay in May. He played in two exhibition games and led the NFL with four sacks in the preseason. Pyburn played his first three college seasons at Florida and spent last season at LSU.

Harden signed as an undrafted free agent with Cleveland in May before getting waived Aug. 3. He then signed with Seattle three days later and appeared in one exhibition game, gaining 1 yard on two carries and recovering a fumbled punt. He was waived Aug. 17 by the Seahawks. Harden played three years in college at UCLA and finished last season at SMU. He rushed for 2,445 yards and 21 TDs in 44 career games.

Harden is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and is reportedly interested in playing for Missouri or Kentucky.

Wright originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Philadelphia in the spring but was waived by the Eagles on Aug. 10. He was claimed by Cleveland the next day and spent nearly two weeks with the Browns before getting waived again on Aug. 23. Wright didn't appear in a preseason game. Wright played his first two seasons in college at Virginia Tech and final two at Mississippi. He had 113 catches for 1,603 yards and five TDs in 47 career games.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and wants to play for his former Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

Harris originally signed as an undrafted free agent with New Orleans in May and began training camp with the Saints. He was waived on Aug. 8 before the first preseason game. Harris played four seasons in college at Ole Miss and had 5 1/2 sacks in 52 games. He had two of his career-high nine tackles for loss last season in the College Football Playoff.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and also wants to play for Kiffin at LSU.

Hankerson originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Miami in the spring and began camp with the Dolphins. He was waived on Aug. 10 and signed a week later with Seattle. He spent one week with the Seahawks before getting waived again on Aug. 24. Hankerson had five carries for 10 yards and two catches for 9 yards for Seattle in an exhibition game against Tennessee on Aug. 23. Hankerson played his first two seasons in college at Colorado and the final two at Oregon State. He rushed for 2,761 yards and 28 TDs in 44 career games and had back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons for the Beavers.

Hankerson is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and could try to return to Oregon State.

title: Aaron Judge to join Yankees on West Coast trip as rehab progression continues
description: NEW YORK — Aaron Judge is set to join the Yankees on this week’s West Coast road trip as he continues to work his way back from a broken rib. Judge has been progressing through baseball activities — including throwing from 100 feet and taking indoor, overhand batting practice — but had not yet faced high-velocity pitching. “I’m sure he’ll be ramped up and a lot more involved in the pregame ...
fullText:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge is set to join the Yankees on this week's West Coast road trip as he continues to work his way back from a broken rib.

Judge has been progressing through baseball activities — including throwing from 100 feet and taking indoor, overhand batting practice — but had not yet faced high-velocity pitching.

"I'm sure he'll be ramped up and a lot more involved in the pregame stuff," manager Aaron Boone said Sunday of the plan for Judge on the road trip.

"Hopefully out there, [Judge will] start to get on velocity and things like that, be part of the pregame stuff, and just get more entrenched into getting ready to come back."

The Yankees are set to begin a three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels in Anaheim on Monday, then play the Padres in San Diego over the weekend.

They have not shared a timeline for Judge to return, but with the Yankees in the thick of a playoff race, the slugger said last week that he would prefer to forgo a minor-league rehab assignment.

"Why waste at-bats?" Judge, 34, said Thursday. "Why waste anything down in a minor-league game? I've been doing this for a while now, and I've got a sense of what I need to do on the field and how to manage it, so why waste at-bats in Double-A or Triple-A?"

Judge has been sidelined since May 31 due to a right rib stress fracture — an injury he suspects occurred more than a month earlier when he dove in right field during a game in Houston.

The three-time American League MVP is hitting .248 with 17 home runs and a .907 OPS in 59 games this season. In his absence, Spencer Jones and Heliot Ramos are sharing time in right field.

In 2023, Judge didn't play in any minor-league rehab games before returning from a toe injury that had kept him out for about two months.

There are four weeks remaining in the regular season.

"I'm gonna play smart," Judge said last week. "I'm gonna still try to go out there and make every play I can, but you gotta be smart, especially near the end of the year now. You know, if it's Game 7 of the World Series, I'll definitely be diving, so I don't think that'll ever change. But just be smart the next couple weeks as we get back, and we'll be good."

title: Broncos waive former Texas A&M LB, hope to add him to practice squad

fullText:
As roster churning continues across the NFL in the days following cut‑down day, teams that waived players they liked but couldn't fit on the initial 53‑man roster now have to wait and see whether those players clear waivers. Unlike vested veterans who become free agents immediately, waived players must pass through the waiver wire before the team that released them can re‑sign them to the practice squad.

Making an NFL roster as an undrafted free agent is always a long shot. Roughly 15% of UDFAs make an initial 53‑man roster, and about 25% land on a practice squad. That means the majority never appear in a regular‑season game. For York, the Broncos have made it clear they want him back on the practice squad if he goes unclaimed.

York has always been an underdog, and this is simply the next test in a career built on proving doubters wrong. If he clears waivers, he'll have another opportunity to continue that journey in Denver.

title: Metayer's rebound goal gives the Spirit a 1-0 victory over Bay FC

fullText:
Paige Metayer scored on the rebound after Trinity Rodman's shot hit the crossbar to lift the Washington Spirit to a 1-0 victory over Bay FC on Sunday.

In the day's later National Women's Soccer League match, the Seattle Reign slipped by the Houston Dash 1-0.

Rodman collected the ball just beyond Audi Field's middle-third late in first-half stoppage time, drove to the corner of the 6-yard-box and struck the bottom of the crossbar. Metayer crashed the goal line and knocked in the rebound before goalkeeper Jordan Silkowitz could react.

Rodman was later on the receiving end of a late tackle from Bay FC's Maddie Moreau, who earned a yellow card. Washington's Metayer and Gabrielle Carle were also given yellows.

Bay FC (6-11-4) kept pace with the Spirit (12-6-4), matching Washington's four shots on goal and keeping a slight edge in possession. Bay committed just five fouls to Washington's 10 as the injury-riddled Spirit secured its first victory in five matches.

Maddie Dahlien scored the sixth winner of her career at Lumen Field, breaking through in the 52nd minute to lift the Seattle Reign (10-8-4) past the Houston Dash (7-11-5).

She had a team-high five shots, four of those on target. Maddie Mercado provided the assist, sending a well-placed cross beyond the reach of goalkeeper Jane Campbell and into Dahlien's path.

Campbell made four saves, including a one-on-one stop against Dahlien in the 80th minute when she sprawled to deny the Reign forward on a counterattack.

Both teams will soon lose key players to the United States Under-20 women's national team, which will compete at the U-20 Women's World Cup in Poland. Seattle's Ainsley McCammon and Houston's Linda Ullmark are expected to join the squad in September before returning to their clubs.

title: Purple Row After Dark: What are you watching around MLB this September?
description: The Rockies may be struggling, but the rest of baseball is giving us plenty to watch.
fullText:
For most of the season, my attention stays pretty firmly on the Colorado Rockies.

That will not change down the stretch, but the losses are starting to stack up again. The Rockies are 4-11 over their last 15 games, and that can get frustrating.

Sometimes it is nice to look up and see what else is happening around baseball, and as the calendar nears September, it is a good time to do exactly that.

Fortunately, baseball's final month looks to hold plenty of intrigue, both in the standings and on individual leaderboards.

While not a particularly good division, the AL West might be the least settled division race of all. Houston sits at 69-68, just one game above .500. Texas is 67-70 and two games back, while Seattle sits at 64-73 and five games out. Houston does not exactly look interested in running away with the division, but Texas and Seattle have not shown much desire to take it from them, either. Personally, I would not mind a Houston-less October.

Then there are the White Sox. Two years removed from losing 121 games, Chicago is 72-64 and leads the 69-68 Guardians by 3.5 games in the AL Central. Can they finish off one of baseball's more unexpected division titles — or can the Rockies perhaps play spoilers in the final days of the season?

Both Wild Card races still leave room for a late surprise. Cleveland holds the final AL spot, but Baltimore is just one game back, Toronto is 1.5 out and Texas sits two back. In the NL, Arizona holds the final spot by just a half-game over San Diego, while Miami remains 3.5 games out.

Meanwhile, Yordan Alvarez enters the stretch run hitting .320 with 37 home runs and 93 RBI. He leads the American League in all three categories, putting a Triple Crown firmly within reach.

On the mound, Jacob Misiorowski owns a 1.73 ERA with 222 strikeouts in 151 innings. If he can stay below 2.00 and reach 250 strikeouts, he would be the first pitcher to accomplish both since Jacob deGrom in 2018.

And the National League home run race is of particular interest to us Rockies fans. Kyle Schwarber leads the league with 40, Matt Olson has 37, and Hunter Goodman is tied with Pete Crow-Armstrong at 36. Goodman has already produced two three-homer games this season, so we know he can hit them in bunches.

Those are a few things I will be watching.

title: SEC’s fight to block former pros could decide how college football enforces rules
description: LSU commitments Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris have reignited the SEC's fight over whether former professional players can return to college football.
fullText:
The college football season got underway in Week 0, but off-field battles are still brewing. This time, an entire conference is fighting for the power to enforce its established rules regarding professional athletes returning to college athletics.

The SEC was told by a Baton Rouge, Louisiana, judge that the conference could not punish schools that sign former professional players. College football has done everything it can to draw a clear line between itself and professional sports.

Now, the SEC is getting ready to rumble. In court, of course. The SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey will contest the ruling in court Thursday and are prepared to fight back.

MORE: College football analyst doubts Dae'Quan Wright will ever take the field for LSU

"The order entered against the SEC and Commissioner Sankey is a temporary restraining order, not a final ruling on the merits. The SEC and Commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs' petition at Thursday morning's hearing and defend the SEC's rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions." The SEC said in a statement via CBS Sports.

Jul 20, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris have both committed to the LSU Tigers through the transfer portal. While Harris spent only a short time with the New Orleans Saints, Wright saw game action with the Cleveland Browns. The Browns claimed Wright off waivers on August 11 and he appeared in preseason games.

Harris did not appear in any preseason contests, but he and Wright both declared for the 2026 NFL Draft. They also went through the full draft process and became undrafted free agents. After yet another bizarre ruling, both players regained their college eligibility and decided to enter the transfer portal.

MORE: Can USC quarterback Jayden Maiava take Fernando Mendoza-like leap in 2026?

Both played at Ole Miss in 2025 under current LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. In typical Kiffin fashion, he has been vocal in opposing the conference's efforts to prevent the two players from playing.

Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Mississippi Rebels tight end Dae'Quan Wright (8) scores a touchdown against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The reality is that this has simply gone too far. When a player declares for the NFL Draft, that should undoubtedly end his college football career. Instead, we have reached a point where players are looking for a judge who will give them what they want.

There is no true merit to these rulings beyond arguments that are enough to get an injunction granted. The Brendan Sorsby case was just the beginning. If college sports cannot enforce their rules, what will be next?

The fate of this line in the sand could rest on the shoulders of the SEC.

title: 6 takeaways after Broncos set initial 53-man roster
description: The Broncos set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. Here are six quick takeaways.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos had a busy weekend.

Denver's front office made 38 moves over the last two days to get down to an initial 53-man roster.

"Every year is hard, regardless of your depth," general manager George Paton said on Sunday evening. "This is a tough day. It's always challenging. This year, I think we spent more time on this roster going through a lot of different scenarios with a lot of these players that were released. It's a puzzle. It's ongoing. Now we're building the practice squad, we're looking at the wire tonight, obviously. So it's fluid, and yet yes, this was a tough roster to make."

With that noted, here are six quick takeaways from Paton's post-cuts conference call.

1. Broncos injury report: Offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo was moved from the active/physically unable to perform list to the reserve/PUP list, and tight end Caleb Lohner and offensive tackle Frank Crum were placed on short-term injured reserve. All three players will be eligible to return after four games, but they might not all be ready that quickly. Paton roughly estimated Lohner could return in October.

2. Justin Joly among cut draft picks: Denver cut three members of their 2026 NFL draft class: tight end Justin Joly (fifth round), linebacker Red Murdock (seventh round) and safety Miles Scott (seventh round). All three players will likely be top targets for the Broncos' practice squad — if they clear waivers. "You always worry about the guys you want to bring back that they could get claimed," Paton said. "If they do, like we told them, we're going to give them a hug and wish them the best. That's part of it; that's part of the league. It's a risk when you put guys out there. It's just part of it."

3. Sam Ehlinger returns as QB3: After not making the initial 53-man roster last summer, Ehlinger has made the active roster in 2026. "Sam is a big part of this quarterback room," Paton said. "We didn't want to lose him, and we felt we were going to lose him [if he was cut]. He's too important to our team and just didn't want to risk doing that. Obviously, the game he played the other night was outstanding. We love the room. We're going to keep the room together." Denver didn't want to take the risk of attempting to bump Ehlinger down to the practice squad because other clubs likely would have offered him a spot on their active roster.

4. Jaleel McLaughlin's moving on: After being waived on Sunday, this feels like the end of McLaughlin's time in Denver (he posted a goodbye message on Instagram). Paton said choosing between Tyler Badie and McLaughlin was one of the hardest and one of the final cut decisions the Broncos made. Paton noted that special teams and "third-down ability" were two key factors. Badie, unlike McLaughlin, is heavily involved in the kicking game, and he's a reliable pass blocker.

5. Broncos get roster flexibility with two cuts: Two of Denver's notable cuts were fullback Adam Prentice and long snapper Mitchell Fraboni. Because they are vested veterans, neither player is subject to the NFL's waiver wire. The Broncos plan to re-sign both players to their practice squad, and they can be elevated to the game-day roster up to three times. Eventually, Prentice and Fraboni will be fully promoted to the active roster. In the meantime, Denver has some early-season roster flexibility with those two on the practice squad.

6. Jonathon Cooper placed on exempt list: The NFL placed Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday, which means he can't practice or play in games until the league makes an updated ruling. In the meantime, the Broncos still have Nik Bonitto, Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman at outside linebacker. Paton said Denver likes their OLB room, but he also acknowledged the team will look for depth. "[W]e'll be looking a little bit, looking on the practice squad and we'll be looking around," Paton said. "You can never have enough pass rushers, so we'll kind of see how that goes."

Up next are waiver claims on Monday morning. After claims are processed, the Broncos can begin building a 17-player practice squad for the 2026 NFL season (expect Prentice and Fraboni to be among the first signings).

title: 7 players on 49ers roster who could be headed for IR
description: The San Francisco 49ers have their initial 53-man roster, but now they'll make some additional moves to free up roster spots.
fullText:
Even after an avalanche of roster moves at Sunday's deadline for final cuts, the San Francisco 49ers still have plenty of work to do on their roster.

With a handful of players likely returning to the club in some capacity, the 49ers will need to free up some roster spots. They could do that via the outright release of someone who made the first version of the 53-man roster. They can also create roster spots by placing players from the 53-man group on IR. Players who are on the roster and then go on IR can be designated for return. Players who are placed on IR before final cuts can't return, save for the maximum two players who are allowed to be given return designations.

One key with the return designations that come down at final cuts is that they count toward the maximum eight IR returns for the season, even if they never come off IR. That forces teams to be strategic with how they utilize those IR slots on cutdown day.

Now that we know what the 49ers' initial 53-man roster looks like, and we know they'll need to clear up a couple of roster spots, here are seven players who could be tagged for IR now that they've made the initial roster:

Lowe suffered a high ankle sprain early in camp. There's a chance he'll be ready for the season opener or within the first couple weeks of the season which would allow him to avoid the minimum four-week absence that comes with an IR stint. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed to reporters Lowe was an IR candidate at final cuts. He may still be one now that he's on the team.

It's unclear exactly how severe Height's ankle injury is. There's a chance he's ready to go for the season opener, but given that he missed the 49ers' preseason finale it's worth wondering whether the team will shut him down for the first few weeks to ensure he's fully healthy when he does return. Keep an eye on his participation in the three days leading up to the team's departure for Australia.

Gifford has been dealing with a hamstring injury since early in training camp. Those injuries can be tricky to deal with and it wouldn't be a surprise if the 49ers determine some additional time off would be helpful for the special teams ace. With seven linebackers on the roster it would make sense that at least one is headed for an injured list.

Put Martin in the same boat as Gifford, although he suffered his injury in the second preseason game. That puts him on a different timeline than Gifford. The severity of the injuries will matter here, but with a logjam at LB Martin could be on his way to IR.

It was a rough camp for Hobbs who had a real shot to carve out a role. He came back from one injury and quickly hurt his groin and hasn't practiced since early in camp. Given his lack of practice time he's a prime IR candidate who may or may not ever get the return designation.

Prysock hurt his shoulder in the preseason finale and Shanahan said he was a candidate to go on IR. Perhaps additional testing over the last few days showed he won't need to be out an extended period. An injury late in the preseason could be tough from a timeline standpoint, though, and Prysock may head to IR if the team determines he needs more than a week or two to get right.

It would appear Mustapha is trending toward a return since he made the initial roster and hasn't participated since the early days of camp. Hamstrings are tricky, though, and he's a potential starter once he's healthy. The 49ers won't likely want to rush him back into action.

fullText:
After having his postseason hopes ripped from his arms Saturday at Daytona, Trackhouse Racing's Shane van Gisbergen took to social media to comment on the evening and his season as a whole.

"Shame to miss out on the chase," he said on X. "One night doesn't sum up our year but we haven't been good enough, so it's been cool to be close anyway."

The Australian-born driver has been nothing short of dominant on road courses since his NASCAR debut in 2023, and in years past, winning a single race with lefties and righties would be good enough to qualify for the playoffs. But under this year's new Chase format, all drivers had to qualify on points; so despite having a pair of wins under his belt in 2026, SVG came up one spot shy of the postseason.

Despite the bitter end, van Gisbergen expressed gratitude for his obvious improvement on oval tracks this year and thanked everyone on his team.

"As a team we've struggled this year but proud to have been able to match my teammates on the ovals and to have stepped up this year," he said. "Obviously wanted to be in that chase and we just didn't make it. Thanks to the @TeamTrackhouse #97 team for their hard work, good to get a first oval stage win at least and there's still a few races to come for the year."

van Gisbergen joins his teammates Ross Chastain and Connor Zilisch on the outside looking in of the Chase cutline, spelling major trouble for a team that was, once upon a time, an up-and-coming juggernaut. Still, van Gisbergen remains a class act through clearly unstable times at Trackhouse.

title: Steven Alker storms back to top Michael Block, win The Ally Challenge
description: Steven Alker fired four straight birdies to secure his 13th PGA Tour Champions win at The Ally Challenge in Michigan.
fullText:
GRAND BLANC, MI — Steven Alker crashed the Block party.

Alker made four consecutive birdies on the back nine en route to a final-round 4-under 68 to hold off a big-name leaderboard and run away with The Ally Challenge crown at Warwick Hills Golf & Country Club on Sunday, Aug. 30. It was Alker's 13th victory on the 50-and-older PGA Tour Champions tour — including his third this season and his second in as many weeks.

Alker, 55, from New Zealand, took sole possession of the lead with a birdie at the par-4 12th hole, then expanded it with a two-putt birdie at the par-5 13th hole, as Michael Block, the one-time viral sensation, made bogey.

"Perfect number," Alker said of his second-shot, 3-wood approach from 245 yards into the 13th hole, where the momentum really swung to his corner. "Worked out well."

Alker made birdies at Nos. 14 and 15 (the latter on a 60-foot putt), too, as he seized yet another title and bolstered his standing in the season-long Charles Schwab Cup points race, which he's won twice before. Alker won for the second time in Michigan, having won the Senior PGA Championship in 2022 at Harbor Shores in Benton Harbor.Alker entered Sunday's final round two shots back of Block, the 50-year-old PGA Tour Champions rookie who was looking for his first win in any PGA Tour-sanctioned tournament.

But Block was stuck in the mud during the rain-delayed final round as highly acclaimed golfers made charges from all corners of the course.

"Steven Alker showed me a couple things I need to do," Block said. "I played a little bit different golf than I did the first two days because I was nervous; I had never been there before. So, it was a learning experience for me."

Still, Block was just one shot back standing on the 13th tee, and he found the fairway.

His tee shot at 13 was on the right side of the fairway, and he was blocked out of the green by an overhanging tree. He tried to play a cut, but double-crossed his 3 wood and pulled it well left of the green. That left him short-sided. He left his third shot short of a greenside bunker, then put his fourth shot in the bunker. He got up and down for bogey, but with Alker's birdie, he walked off the green trailing by three.Block, who was making just his fifth start on PGA Tour Champions, made birdie at the par-3 14th, but bogeyed the par-4 15th, and his first title will have to wait. His last five wins of note anywhere were at the Southern California PGA Championship. He's best-known for one swing: a hole-in-one in the final round of the 2023 PGA Championship, playing alongside Rory McIlroy.Alker finished at 15 under to win by three strokes over World Golf Hall-of-Famer and two-time U.S. Open champ Retief Goosen, who shot a hard-charging 8-under 64 on Sunday. Goosen clawed his way into a tie for the lead on the back nine, but missed short birdie putts at Nos. 13 and 14 to halt the momentum."It's been a great week," Goosen said. "Obviously wasn't good enough."

Stewart Cink, the 2024 and 2025 Ally Challenge winner and a former British Open champion, shot a final-round 67 and finished 11 under, tied for third with Block (74), who now gets into the next tournament, and Greg Chalmers (69).

Finishing sixth at 10 under was former Masters winner Angel Cabrera (71), and finishing tied for seventh at 9 under was Padraig Harrington (73), a three-time major champion who won the PGA Championship at Oakland Hills in 2008.

Brandt Jobe, father of Tigers pitcher Jackson Jobe, finished tied for 12th at 8 under, after a Sunday 69. The highlight of the week was catching up with his son, who he saw pitch Wednesday at Comerica Park.

"It was a busy week, needless to say," Jobe said with a smile. "Overall, a very nice week. A busy week."

Wyandotte's Justin Hicks, who Tuesday-qualified into the Ally, finished tied for 27th in his fourth start on PGA Tour Champions. George McNeill, whose caddie is Lake Orion's Tom Gillis (formerly a PGA Tour and Champions player), finished tied for 44th.The Ally Challenge will return in 2027 for its 10th year, with a one-year extension being finalized just before the 2026 event, tournament officials told The News last week. The 2027 Ally Challenge will be played Aug. 27-29.
